editor.project_settings.no_project: No active project. Create or open a project to edit its settings.
editor.project_settings.target_fps_hint: Target frame rate for the game runtime.
editor.project_settings.gameplay.walk_sp: Player horizontal speed when walking. FPS convention: HL2 ~5.5, CoD ~6, Doom Eternal ~7.
editor.project_settings.gameplay.crouch_: Player horizontal speed when crouching. ~55% of walk in most FPS games.
editor.project_settings.gameplay.jump_ve: Instantaneous vertical velocity on jump. 5.5 m/s = ~1.5 m height with g=9.81.
editor.project_settings.gameplay.jump_co: Minimum time between jumps. Prevents double-jump from holding the key.
editor.project_settings.gameplay.max_hea: Max health value assigned to new entities with HealthComponent (dummies, enemies). The dev can override per-entity in the Inspector.
editor.project_settings.character.half_h: Half the height of the player capsule when standing (total height = (halfH + radius) * 2). Default 0.5 → 1.8m standing with 0.4 radius.
Half the height of the capsule when crouched. Default 0.1 → 1.0m crouched.
editor.project_settings.character.radius: Player capsule radius (does not change between standing/crouch). Default 0.4 — fits through standard FPS doorways.
editor.project_settings.character.eye_he: Vertical offset of the eyes from the capsule center when standing. Default 0.7.
Vertical offset of the eyes when crouched. Default 0.3.
editor.project_settings.character.headbo: Headbob oscillations per second while walking. Default 3.5 Hz — F2H41: realistic human stride (~1.6m per step at 5.5 m/s).
Camera sway height while walking in meters. Default 0.05. Above 0.1 feels drunk; below 0.02 is barely perceptible.
editor.map_tools.snap.current_step_hint: Active snap step (cycle with Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Shift+ScrollWheel over an ortho viewport).
editor.map_tools.snap.steps_hint: List of available steps. Open world: large steps; detailed interior: small steps.
editor.map_tools.snap.add_step: Add a new step (default = last x 2)
editor.map_tools.snap.vertex_threshold_h: Maximum NDC distance for the cursor to stick to a vertex. 0.02 = ~8 px at 800 px height. Higher = more generous snap.
editor.map_tools.snap.broadphase_hint: Minimum world-units distance for snap broadphase. Only vertices of brushes within this expanded AABB are enumerated.
editor.user_preferences.editor.camera_fa: Maximum visible distance from the editor orbital camera + Play camera. Default 1000 m. Lower it if your map is small for better Z precision; raise to 10000+ for open-world maps. Applies live (no restart).
editor.user_preferences.editor.camera_ma: Maximum distance you can pull back from the target with the wheel. Default 500 m. Raise it if you can't see a large building in full. Doesn't affect min zoom (still 0.5 m).
editor.user_preferences.editor.ortho_ini: Frustum height in world units when a new ortho viewport (Top/Front/Side) is created. Open world goes up; detailed interior goes down. The live wheel zoom modifies the running camera state, not this default.
editor.user_preferences.editor.ortho_zoo: Multiplier per wheel tick on the ortho camera. 1.10 = each wheel zooms ~9 %. Higher = more aggressive; lower = finer.
editor.user_preferences.editor.gizmo_arm: Length of the translate/scale gizmo arms in screen pixels. Calibrated for 1080p at 60 px; bump to ~100 on 4K.
editor.user_preferences.editor.gizmo_rot: Target on-screen size of the rotate gizmo ring in pixels. Constant on screen (does not scale with camera distance).
editor.user_preferences.editor.click_dra: Pixel distance the mouse must move before a held left click counts as a drag. Raise this if your trackpad fires accidental drags on click.
editor.user_preferences.editor.thumbnail: Size in pixels of the 3D mesh thumbnails in the Asset Browser. Raise for more detail on 4K displays; lower if you have many meshes and notice a hitch when opening the panel. Thumbnails are cached on disk across sessions.
editor.user_preferences.editor.hover_pre: Milliseconds the cursor must stay still over an Asset Browser thumbnail before the expanded preview (large mesh/sphere + asset metadata) appears. 0 = instant; raise this if the tooltip pops up accidentally while browsing.
editor.user_preferences.editor.stats_ove: Number of drawMesh calls per frame (opaque PBR + skinned + shadow). Useful to spot poor batching.
Triangles submitted to the GPU per frame. Key metric for geometry budget.
VRAM used by the process (via NVX_gpu_memory_info on NVIDIA). Only available on drivers exposing the extension.
Working set (RSS) of the editor process. Constant rise = leak; spikes = thumbnail/asset load.
Active lights participating in the Forward+ binning. Off by default to avoid spamming over the primary chips.
Active entity count in the scene (includes wheel markers and Environment).
editor.user_preferences.editor.profiler_: Frame history kept by the in-engine profiler for avg/min/max and histogram. 240 ≈ 4 seconds at 60 fps. Raise it to see longer trends; lower it if spikes average out.
editor.user_preferences.editor.toasts.en: Ephemeral notifications in the bottom-right corner when saving, opening a map, etc. Turn off for silent mode (logs still flow into the Console).
editor.user_preferences.editor.toasts.li: How long each toast stays on screen before fading. 3000 ms (3 s) felt natural; raise it if you miss messages; lower to 1500 if toasts stack up.
Automatically saves a copy of the map every N minutes into .autosave/. Only writes if there are unsaved changes. Turn off if you work on slow filesystems.
How often to trigger autosave. 5 = same default as Unity/Unreal. Raise it if you don't want periodic I/O; lower it if you realize you lose more work than that interval.

editor.panel.lua_api.intro: Bindings available for scripts assigned via ScriptComponent. The system calls `function onUpdate(self, dt)` each frame for the entity that owns the script.
editor.panel.lua_api.hud_intro: Global game state (HP/Ammo/paused). Visible in the Play Mode HUD (editor) or in MoodPlayer (standalone). The state lives in GameState (singleton) — all scripts share the same instance.
editor.panel.lua_api.log_intro: Logging that appears in the editor's Console panel (channel `script`). Useful for debug — do not use `print()` (Lua print goes to stdout which the editor does not capture).
editor.panel.lua_api.lifecycle_intro: The engine calls these functions on the script. Define them in the global `.lua`; ScriptSystem invokes them by name.
editor.panel.lua_api.hot_reload: Hot-reload: if the .lua file changes on disk, ScriptSystem re-runs the chunk in the same sol::state. Script globals persist across reloads.

editor.panel.narrative_intro.title: Narrative Workspace
editor.panel.narrative_intro.heading: Sub-phase 2.5 — Game systems (in progress)
editor.panel.narrative_intro.body: This workspace is the home of the upcoming game-content editors: Dialog Editor, Quest Editor, and Inventory. Right now you're seeing the Node Graph Sandbox — the foundation infrastructure that the Dialog and Quest editors will be built on top of. Use it to test the framework (pan/zoom, sockets, connections, undo, save/load) but be aware: this is plumbing, not a final tool.
editor.panel.narrative_intro.item_dialog: Dialog Editor (F2H47): each node = a line spoken by an NPC. Connections = options the player picks. Wire it to a NPC in your scene via a DialogComponent that points to a .mooddialog file you'll build visually here.
editor.panel.narrative_intro.item_quest: Quest Editor: each node = an objective. Connections = dependencies. Quests trigger from world events (entering an area, picking up an item, killing an enemy tag).
editor.panel.narrative_intro.item_invent: Inventory (separate UI, not node-graph): item asset browser with 3D preview + grid/list/equipment-slot component you attach to entities. Pickup/drop wired to physics triggers + the HUD interact prompt.
editor.panel.narrative_intro.footer: All three systems are engine-grade primitives: data-driven (.mooddialog/.moodquest/.mooditem assets), no hardcoded gameplay semantics, Lua hooks for game logic. They serve any genre.
